blocks.text: Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC

Ashcombe Advisory Partners advises mid-market public companies, and private companies preparing for a public listing, on corporate communications and investor relations. Our work concerns how a company explains itself to the audiences whose judgment matters most to it: investors and analysts, the financial and trade press, and its own employees.
We are a small firm by design. The advisors a client meets at the outset are the ones who carry the work through, and we accept an engagement only where we can offer that continuity.
The character of the practice

A large part of what we do is correspondence. We draft messaging, route it for approval, and keep an announcement's timeline in order, and most of that takes place by email in the days and hours before a company speaks publicly.

In our experience, the preparation around an announcement matters as much as the text of the release. We therefore give a considerable share of each engagement to the questions a company should expect, the answers its own records can support, and the order in which its audiences ought to hear the news.
Lines of service

Our advice is organized around the services set out below. They overlap in practice, and a single engagement will often draw on more than one of them. The descriptions are indicative rather than exhaustive, and the scope of any engagement is agreed with the client at the outset.

rows: A single, consistent account of the company's strategy and prospects, suitable for management, the board, and the investor materials alike
Earnings materials, talking points for management, preparation for analyst calls, and the planning of investor outreach
The drafting and timing of releases, wire distribution and embargo arrangements, and the handling of press inquiries
Remarks, letters, and prepared answers that a senior executive delivers in his or her own name
A review of how the company is presently understood, and counsel when a matter becomes public before the company is ready to address it

blocks.text: Illustrative engagements

We describe a client's work only after the engagement has concluded. The two examples below are offered to show the range of the practice; they are illustrations, not a list of the companies we have advised.

For {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}, we developed a corporate positioning: one account of the business that its leadership, its investor materials, and its dealings with the press could all draw on. The work began with interviews across the leadership team and a review of how the company had been described in coverage, and it concluded with a positioning statement and the supporting messages beneath it.

For {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}, we conducted an investor relations program across successive reporting periods. We prepared earnings materials and management talking points, readied the company's spokespeople for analyst calls, and helped the company describe its results consistently from one period to the next.
How we conduct an engagement

Each engagement opens with a signed engagement letter and a kickoff memo, which together record the scope, the people involved on both sides, and the decisions the client reserves to itself. The work then proceeds largely by email, in threads that keep a plain record of what was proposed, what was approved, and by whom.

Nothing we draft is released without the client's express approval. Where an announcement involves an embargo or wire distribution, we coordinate the timing with the client's legal and finance teams and confirm each step before the next one begins.
Leadership

The firm is led by Julie Hill, Managing Partner, who reviews each client announcement before it is released. Her own background is in corporate investor relations, and her review of a draft begins with how it will sound to the analysts and investors who will hear it. Each client relationship is also overseen by a partner, who remains its point of escalation for as long as the engagement runs.
Initial inquiries

A company considering an engagement is welcome to write to Julie Hill, who will arrange a first conversation with the advisors best placed to help. It is useful if that first note describes, even briefly, what the company has ahead of it, so that the right people take part in the conversation.

Onboarding Record: Kimberly Le

Kimberly Le joined Ashcombe Advisory Partners last week as a Communications Analyst in the Advisory group, and we are very glad to have her with us. She brings a close interest in how stories travel online, which is an increasing part of what our clients ask us to watch on their behalf. This record, prepared by Julie Hill, notes the role she has taken up, where it sits within the practice, and the arrangements we have agreed for her first weeks.
The role and where it sits

Kimberly's work centers on monitoring press, online, and social coverage for the companies we advise, and on the short briefing notes our advisors read on the way into a client call. She reports to Michael Morris, Partner, who runs the advisory bench day to day and will decide which client relationships she supports first. Because those notes often reach an advisor minutes before a conversation begins, we value an accurate source and a clear summary well above speed or volume of commentary.
The first weeks

Her laptop, firm email account, and remote access are in place, and the operations team is taking her through the shared drive, our filing conventions, and the practice of keeping each engagement's correspondence within its own thread. For the present she will work beside the advisor on each relationship she joins, learning how that client's coverage is followed before she takes the monitoring on herself. Client coverage and draft materials are confidential, and she will discuss them only with colleagues working on the relationship concerned.

We would ask Kimberly to raise a story with the responsible advisor as soon as she sees it begin to move, even where she is not yet certain it will matter, and to keep her notes internal until an advisor has reviewed them. Her first scheduled step is a review with Michael Morris of the monitoring she has set up so far, at which the two of them will agree the relationships she will cover next.
Nancy Suarez, Communications Associate

Nancy Suarez joined us last week as a Communications Associate in the Advisory group, and it is a pleasure to welcome her. Julie Hill has prepared this note for the personnel file, recording what Nancy's role involves, where she sits within the practice, and what has been arranged for the period ahead.

Nancy is responsible for the mechanics of client announcements: wire distribution, the timing of embargoes, and coordination with a client's legal and finance teams on the day a release goes out. She reports to Michael Morris, Partner, and on each release she will work with the advisor who leads it. The work depends on every step being confirmed as it happens, and we would ask her to say so plainly whenever an instruction is unclear.
Arrangements agreed

items: Her laptop, firm email account, and remote access were ready on her first day, and the operations team is walking her through the shared drive and the folders kept for each release.
On her first releases she will keep the checklist herself while the advisor leading the release confirms each step, so that she learns the sequence before she runs a release day on her own.
The firm's wire service accounts and media distribution lists are held centrally, and she will be given her own access once she has completed a release under supervision.
Embargoed drafts and release timings are confidential until the client issues the announcement, and are discussed only with colleagues working on that engagement.

blocks.text: Her first step is to go through the firm's release checklist line by line with Michael Morris, after which she will keep her own working copy for every release she handles.
Good morning Michael and Kimberly,

Timesheets for this week are due by close of business today, since the office is closed on Monday for the holiday. I checked the system before submitting my own, and yours are the two still open for the advisory group. Kimberly, your Thursday hours are saved but not yet submitted. Michael, yours just needs Wednesday filled in. Once both are in, the week can be closed out.
If it is easier, reply with your hours and I will enter them for you before I leave today.
Regards
Hi John,

Thank you for agreeing to take my turn on the holiday coverage rota, which puts you on the main line and the shared inbox on Tuesday morning while I am still traveling back, and I will take one of your turns later in the summer so that the arrangement evens out between us. I have updated the shared calendar to show the swap under both our names, and my out-of-office reply now directs anyone who writes to me to you.

Most of what comes in that morning will be routine and can wait until I am back at my desk in the afternoon. If something cannot wait, please forward it to me by email with a line on top, and I will deal with it as soon as I am off the road.
Sincerely
